compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc B580 (Xe2/Battlemage), SIMD16/32 lanes, XMX matrix engines available. HLSL cs_6_10 with Direct3D Linear Algebra FP16 thread vector-matrix supported.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Y = X @ W^T + b. M=32768, K=256, N=256, fp16. ~1.07 GFLOPs per batch row pair; total ~4.3 GFLOPS. Compute-light per row; bandwidth-bound on input X reads and output Y writes; weight matrix is 128 KiB (reusable).
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: If linalg intrinsic path doesn't map to XMX, FLOPs may bottleneck on FMA throughput.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Reads: X=16 MiB, W=128 KiB (broadcast/reused), b=512 B. Writes: Y=16 MiB. Weight reuse factor = BATCH=32768. Bandwidth dominated by X read + Y write (~32 MiB total).
memory_bandwidth.risk: Without weight reuse via cache/shared, repeated W reloads would dominate.

register_pressure.notes: Per-thread accumulator: 256 fp16 outputs would be heavy. Need to tile per-thread output (e.g., one row -> 8/16 outputs per thread, or one wave produces one row's 256 outputs via 32 lanes * 8 outs).
register_pressure.risk: Holding entire 256-element accumulator in registers per thread is too large; tile or distribute across lanes.

nodes.notes: 1) Classification: dense GEMM (M=32768, K=N=256), fp16, bias-add fused. Single output per (m,n): sum_k X[m,k]*W[n,k] + b[n]. Dense, no reductions across batch. 2) Canonical: Y[m,n] = b[n] + sum_{k=0..255} X[m,k]*W[n,k]. K-reduction; m,n independent. 3) Layout: X row-major (M,K), W row-major (N,K) i.e. weight[out,in], b (N). All fp16 raw ByteAddressBuffer. Dominant traffic: X reads (16MB), Y writes (16MB). W (128KB) is fully reused BATCH times -> stage in groupshared or rely on L2. b (512B) tiny, can be cached/broadcast. 4) Regimes: (a) bandwidth-bound -> need W reuse and coalesced X/Y access; (b) compute-bound if linalg/XMX engages and BW is saturated; (c) latency-bound if too few groups. 5) Knobs: tile size (rows per group), how many output cols per thread, W staging (groupshared vs SRV reads via L2), wave-cooperative reduction vs per-thread K-loop, use of dx/linalg.h Mul/MulAdd FP16 thread vector-matrix. 6) Skeleton: each threadgroup handles a tile of R rows; cooperatively load W (or a column-tile of W) into groupshared once; each thread/wave computes one row's outputs by reading X[m,:] into registers and doing K-loop accumulations across all 256 N outputs (distributed); write Y[m,:] with bias added. Use [WaveSize(32)]; one wave per row -> each lane handles N/32=8 output columns; X row loaded cooperatively into shared or each lane loads its needed K elements. 7) Families: F1 wave-per-row with W in groupshared (one wave owns one output row, 32 lanes * 8 cols = 256). F2 linalg-thread-vector-matrix using <dx/linalg.h> FP16 Mul (each thread does vec-mat partial). F3 group-per-row-block with X tile staged. Top choice: F1 + linalg intrinsic for the K dot products.

action.description: Implement wave-per-row mapping: one SIMD32 wave produces one output row (256 cols). Each lane owns 8 output columns. Load W (256x256 fp16 = 128KiB) ... but 128KiB exceeds 32KiB groupshared budget. Instead: stream W from SRV (relying on L2 reuse across many waves), keep X row in registers (256 fp16 = 128 regs per wave distributed = 8 per lane), accumulate 8 fp16 outputs per lane via K-loop. Add bias and store.
action.rationale: Maps one independent work unit (row) to one wave; minimal sync; relies on L2 for W reuse (W=128KiB fits easily in L2). Each lane: 8 accumulators, K=256 inner loop. Very register-friendly.
action.title: F1: Wave-per-row, W streamed from L2, X-row in lane registers

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: B580 SIMD32 waves available; WaveReadLaneAt for cross-lane X broadcast.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Each lane: 8 acc * 256 K = 2048 FMAs. Wave: 65536 FMAs per row. K-loop can broadcast X[k] across lanes via WaveReadLaneAt(x_chunk, k%32).
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Wave broadcast overhead per K step; if linalg intrinsic not used, pure scalar FMA throughput must suffice.

memory_bandwidth.notes: W read: 128KiB * (BATCH/waves_per_W_reload). With L2 reuse and 32768 rows, W loaded effectively once per L2 residency window.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If L2 thrashes due to X+Y traffic, W reload cost grows.

register_pressure.notes: Per lane: 8 fp16 X values + 8 fp16 accumulators + a few temps. Very light.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: alternative to F2 (linalg intrinsic) - this uses plain scalar/vector FMA loop. Cannot trivially combine because intrinsic path uses different per-thread matrix shape and ownership.

action.description: Use <dx/linalg.h> FP16 thread-scope vector-matrix multiply. Each thread loads an X row (or chunk) as a fp16 vector and multiplies against a K x Ncol weight tile using linalg::Mul/MulAdd. One thread produces a small output chunk (e.g., 8 or 16 outputs) for one row. Tiles of W loaded cooperatively into groupshared (e.g., a 256x16 fp16 slab = 8KiB) and reused across rows in the group.
action.rationale: Leverages XMX/dedicated matrix path explicitly enabled in the spec for this driver. Highest potential throughput.
action.title: F2: dx/linalg.h FP16 thread vector-matrix multiply

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Spec confirms FP16 thread vector-matrix linalg supported on this Intel driver.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Best HW fit if intrinsic compiles to matrix engine path. Requires careful layout decoration (RowMajor/ColumnMajor) and Pack matrix shape.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Intrinsic shape constraints (K-dim, M-dim multiples) may force padding/restructuring.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Same external traffic as F1; potentially better cache efficiency due to bigger contiguous loads.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Groupshared tile of W only worthwhile if reused across many threads.

register_pressure.notes: Matrix tiles may consume more registers per thread; need to bound output tile width per thread.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: alternative to F1; uses linalg intrinsic instead of scalar loop. Mutually exclusive code paths.

action.description: Threadgroup-per-row-block: group covers R rows (e.g., R=8). Cooperatively stage X tile (R x K = 8*256*2 = 4KiB) and a W column slab (e.g., K x Ncol_tile = 256*32*2 = 16KiB) in groupshared. Each thread computes outputs for one (row, col_tile) chunk. Iterate over N in col tiles.
action.rationale: Maximizes shared-memory reuse of both X and W within a group; good when bandwidth-bound.
action.title: F3: Threadgroup tiled GEMM with X+W groupshared staging

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Groupshared budget 32KiB; X tile + W tile must fit. R=8 rows, Ncol=32 -> ~20KiB.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Group-wide barriers needed after tile loads; risks more synchronization than wave-owned variant.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Each X row read once per group; W column tile read R times reused across rows.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Iterating col tiles re-reads X across N iterations unless kept in shared.

register_pressure.notes: Modest; per-thread accumulators sized by tile.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: alternative to F1/F2 - uses group-wide tiling and explicit shared staging instead of wave-per-row register-only or linalg intrinsic. Combining would defeat the design intent.

kernel_summary: FP16 dense linear projection Y[M,N] = X[M,K] @ W[N,K]^T + b[N] with M=32768, K=N=256. Compute is modest (~4.3 GFLOPs total) and the kernel is bandwidth-leaning: X and Y are 16 MiB each while W is only 128 KiB and is reused BATCH times (ideal L2 / groupshared candidate). Bias is 512 B. Constraints: cs_6_10 raw ByteAddressBuffer/RWByteAddressBuffer, FP16 thread-scope linalg available, groupshared <=32 KiB. Best fit is a wave-owned mapping (one wave per output row, 32 lanes x 8 columns = 256), keeping per-lane accumulators in registers, streaming W through L2 (or a small column-tile in groupshared if needed), and optionally invoking dx/linalg.h FP16 vector-matrix multiply for the K-dot products.
open_questions: Does dx/linalg.h FP16 thread vector-matrix actually lower to XMX on this Intel driver, or to scalar SIMD FMAs?
What are the linalg Mul shape constraints (M/K/N multiples) and required matrix interpretation/layout flags for the (K=256,N=8or16) tile?
Is SIMD32 the default wave size on B580, and does [WaveSize(32)] compile / improve mapping vs SIMD16?
Is W fully cacheable in L2 across the whole dispatch (128 KiB), so we don't need to stage it in groupshared at all?
What groupshared bank/conflict behavior should we expect for fp16 access patterns on Xe2?
Should X[m,:] be loaded into groupshared once per row owner, or kept distributed across lane registers (8 fp16 per lane) and broadcast via WaveReadLaneAt during the K loop?
Is bias best broadcast via a single cooperative load of 256 fp16 (512 B) into groupshared, or read per-lane from SRV?
What dispatch grid (groups in X dimension) best saturates B580 Xe-cores without leaving rows idle (e.g., 32768 rows / waves_per_group)?
